name: YakYak — patch scene dialogue via engine, deliver message

nodes.name: Patch request
nodes.notes: POST { movieId, dialogue, sceneNumber?, deliverTo: { telegram?, discord?, slack? } }. Auth: the header set in the 'YakYak render webhook token' Header Auth credential. One consistent routing story: every channel is a bot credential on the instance, and deliverTo says which channel id each bot posts to — include a key to deliver there, omit it to skip (response reports sent/skipped per channel). deliverTo values: telegram = chat id (from @userinfobot or getUpdates), discord = channel id (right-click channel → Copy Channel ID, Developer Mode on), slack = channel id (C…, channel details dialog).

nodes.name: Call engine

workflowId.cachedResultName: YakYak engine — resolve target, patch or new episode, render, post

nodes.notes: Select the imported workflow.yakyak-engine.json here after import — sub-workflow call replaces the old YAKYAK_ENGINE_URL webhook hop, so no URL or token to configure. Returns { url, movieId, campaignId, mode, changed }. Retry is safe: the engine is diff-aware (same line is a free no-op).

nodes.name: Compose message
nodes.notes: The channel seam: one payload out, one gated parallel branch per destination. Telegram gets a real video upload (≤ ~20 MB via URL fetch), Slack gets a true file upload, Discord gets the caption whose trailing URL auto-embeds.

nodes.name: IF Telegram channel given
nodes.notes: Telegram delivery is opt-in per request (deliverTo.telegram). Absent → skip straight to the merge; response reports deliveries.telegram: skipped.

nodes.name: Send video
nodes.notes: Native Telegram node — the bot token lives in the 'YakYak Telegram bot' credential. sendVideo by URL arrives playable (≤ ~20 MB). Error output (e.g. video too large) falls back to a plain link message.

parameters.jsCode:
const c = $('Compose message').first().json;
return [{ json: { ...c.result, delivered: 'video' } }];

nodes.name: IF Discord channel given
nodes.notes: Discord delivery is opt-in per request (deliverTo.discord). Absent → skip straight to the merge; response reports deliveries.discord: skipped.

nodes.name: Send to Discord

guildId.cachedResultName: (unused — bot-token channel sends route by channel id alone)

nodes.notes: Bot-token delivery so the destination travels with the request (deliverTo.discord = channel id), same pattern as Telegram and Slack. Credential: 'Discord Bot API' named 'YakYak Discord bot' (token from discord.com/developers → your app → Bot → Reset Token); invite the bot to the server with Send Messages permission. The 'Server' field is only used by dropdowns/OAuth2 — bot mode routes purely by channel id, so it stays empty. The caption's trailing mp4 URL auto-embeds. onError=continue: reported as deliveries.discord sent|failed.

nodes.name: IF Slack channel given
nodes.notes: Slack delivery is opt-in per request (deliverTo.slack). Absent → skip straight to the merge — no invisible unshared uploads; response reports deliveries.slack: skipped.

nodes.name: Download video
nodes.notes: Slack has no send-by-URL: the mp4 must be uploaded as bytes, so this fetches it into binary first (held in n8n memory for the hop). Telegram and Discord don't need this — their branches pass the URL through.

nodes.name: Send to Slack
nodes.notes: True video upload (plays inline like Telegram). Credential: 'Slack API' type named 'YakYak Slack bot', Access Token = the xoxb- bot token (scopes: chat:write + files:write); /invite the bot to the channel once. The target channel arrives per request as deliverTo.slack. NOTE: at node version 2.2 the upload uses Slack's new API whose completion call only accepts the SINGULAR channelId option — the plural 'Channel Names or IDs' (channelIds) is silently ignored and the file uploads unshared/invisibly. onError=continue: reported as deliveries.slack sent|failed.

nodes.name: Merge deliveries
nodes.notes: Waits for every channel branch (delivered or skipped) before responding. Adding a channel: bump 'Number of Inputs' and wire both outputs of your IF gate into the new input. Input 1: Telegram. Input 2: Discord. Input 3: Slack.
